sensory.aromaNotes: Mild after processing; commercial Fy Protein is formulated into dairy- and meat-style products
sensory.meatAnalogRationale: Commercial submerged-fermentation mycoprotein (Fy Protein) sold as a meat and dairy analog ingredient; hyphal biomass is texturized similarly to Quorn-style Fusarium protein.
sensory.preparationContext: Heat-inactivated fermented biomass, not a fruiting-body food
sensory.confidenceNotes: Commercial and regulatory dossiers describe use; published sensory scores for the raw biomass remain limited.

morphology.fruitingBodyStructure: Not used in food production; product is filamentous biomass from fermentation
morphology.sporeCharacteristics: Fusarium-type conidia in culture; not part of the food ingredient
morphology.microscopyNotes: Septate branching hyphae typical of Fusarium; 'flavolapis' is an applicant-assigned strain name, not a formally published species epithet

nutrition.limitingAminoAcids: Sulfur amino acids (typical of Fusarium biomass)
nutrition.preparationContext: About 48% protein on a dry-weight basis for Fy Protein biomass (Health Canada novel-food summary)
nutrition.confidenceNotes: Protein figure from the Health Canada novel-food document; amino-acid profile not entered until a primary table is attached.

geographic.nativeRange: Isolated from a geothermal spring, Yellowstone National Park, USA
geographic.cultivatedRegions: Industrial fermentation (Nature's Fynd / The Fynder Group)
geographic.habitat: Environmental isolate; food use is confined to controlled fermentation

strains.availabilityNotes: Deposited as Fusarium oxysporum MK7; later designated Fusarium strain flavolapis.

images.caption: Fusarium microconidia and conidiophores (genus-level morphology; not a photograph of strain flavolapis)

commercialUse.applicationSummary: Fy Protein from Nature's Fynd — fermented Fusarium biomass used in dairy-style and meat-style products in the US and other notified markets.

companies.name: Nature's Fynd (The Fynder Group)
products: dairy-style cream cheese and meatless breakfast items

productionProcess.title: Submerged / surface fermentation
productionProcess.description: Non-viable biomass harvested from Fusarium sp. strain flavolapis, then processed into a protein ingredient.

commercialUse.confidenceNotes: Use and composition summarized from FDA GRAS, Health Canada, and EFSA novel-food documents.

regulatory.notes: FDA GRAS Notice 904 and Health Canada no-objection for Fy Protein. EFSA NDA (Sept 2025, 10.2903/j.efsa.2025.9536) concluded that safety of the biomass cannot be established under the proposed EU uses (insufficient margin of exposure; possible allergenicity). Not a formally published Linnaean species name.

altProteinResearch.title: Safety of the fungal biomass from Fusarium species strain flavolapis as a novel food
altProteinResearch.summary: EFSA NDA opinion on Fy biomass: production and composition were acceptable, but safety could not be established under the proposed EU uses (thyroid findings in a 90-day rat study; insufficient margin of exposure; possible allergenicity).
